title: How to Measure Yourself for a Custom Kurta Set
excerpt: A step-by-step guide to measuring yourself at home for a made-to-measure kurta set or Anarkali – bust, waist, hips, height and more.
body:
A made-to-measure kurta set fits better than any standard size. All you need is a soft measuring tape and five minutes. Ask a friend to help if you can.

## Before you start

Wear light, fitted clothing (or the bra you will wear with the outfit). Stand straight and relaxed, and keep the tape snug but not tight.

## 1. Bust

Measure around the fullest part of your bust, keeping the tape straight across your back.

## 2. Waist

Measure around your natural waist – the narrowest part of your torso, usually just above the belly button.

## 3. Hips

Stand with your feet together and measure around the fullest part of your hips.

## 4. Height

Stand barefoot against a wall and measure from the top of your head to the floor. This helps us set the kurta and pant length.

## 5. Shoulder (optional)

Measure from the edge of one shoulder to the other across the back.

## 6. Sleeve length (optional)

Measure from the shoulder edge to where you want the sleeve to end.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Pulling the tape too tight – leave room for one finger.
- Measuring over thick clothes.
- Guessing your height in shoes.

## Not sure? We'll help

Send your bust, waist and height on WhatsApp and we'll guide you through the rest. If we make a mistake with your measurements, we remake the outfit free.

## Made to measure, shipped worldwide

Every Bahe Kurtiz piece is made in our own Jaipur studio and can be stitched to your measurements at no extra cost. Pieces are made in 5–7 working days and shipped by express courier with tracking, usually arriving in 5–10 business days in the USA, UK, Canada, UAE and Australia.
